563	### D.2 Offer predicates
564	
565	The weld_offer formula is defined as:
566	
567	`weld_offer(seat, s) = ( tool_in_hand(seat) == tool_welder ) AND lit(seat, s) AND in_reach(seat, s) AND ( socket_state(s) == FREE ) AND ( |Pairs(s)| >= 1 )`, with `Pairs(s) = { (a, b) : s IN {a, b} AND host_of(a, b) AND can_attach(a, b) == OK AND docked(a, b, frame_shift_px(a, b)) }` and `host_of` the host rule of D.3 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the earlier form defined `weld_offer` through a host socket `a` that D.3 defined through the same candidate set; the focused socket `s` now seeds the candidate pairs and D.3 only chooses among them)*
568	
569	Derived: the prompt `E . Weld` exists iff `weld_offer` is true. The predicate reads no node or edge accessor, calls neither `can_join_static` nor the full `can_join`, and reads no `surge[]` (MSA-9, MSA-12). The carry lockout (a seat carrying an item gets no channelled verb, PC-7, IA-28) is Interaction's selector, not a term here; a carrying seat therefore never sees the weld prompt and `begin_weld` is a `BUSY` backstop.
570	
571	**Variables:**
572	
573	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
574	|---|---|---|---|---|
575	| `tool_in_hand(seat)` | enum | tool class id | Suit (`tool_welder` is class {1, 9}, slot 2, equipped at start) | The equipped tool |
576	| `lit(seat, s)` | bool | 0 or 1 | Emitter State via Interaction's lit check | The socket subject is lit (lit-only channelled verbs, PC-7) |
577	| `in_reach(seat, s)` | bool | 0 or 1 | Interaction reach geometry, `REACH_PX` 72 | The socket subject is within reach |
578	| `socket_state(s)` | enum | `FREE`, `WELDED`, `CAPPED`, `CUT_OPEN` | Layout (LY-13) | Terminal lifecycle (S3) |
579	| `can_attach(a, b)` | enum | `OK` or one of eight reasons | Layout (LY-14) | The mating verdict |
580	| `frame_shift_px(a, b)` | int pair (px) | on the 24-px grid | Layout `LY D.6` (ASK L3 asks for it as a pure read) | The shift the weld would apply (D.5) |
581	| `docked(a, b, fs)` | bool | 0 or 1 | Body `BDY D.8` | The two bodies already sit at the weld offset with equal velocity |
582	| `Pairs(s)` | set of ordered socket pairs `(a, b)` | 0..`MAX_SOCKETS_PER_SECTION` x `MAX_SECTIONS` in principle; exactly 0 or 1 in MVP | calculated | The ordered pairs that contain the focused socket `s`, put in host order by D.3, and pass both `can_attach` and `docked` |
583	| `weld_offer` | bool | 0 or 1 | calculated | Whether the prompt exists |
584	
585	**Output Range:** boolean. Pure and total: no side effect, no module-body state. In MVP `|Pairs|` is 0 or 1 by authoring (one socket pair); with several candidate pairs `[VS]` D.3 selects the lowest key pair. Per-call cost is O(1) over cached static data (`MSA_WELD_OFFER_BUDGET_US`, set in the spike).
586	
587	**Example:** the seat holds the welder, stands lit within 72 px of `sock_airlock_e`; the socket is `FREE`; `sock_b_w` passes `can_attach` (facings E and W are opposite, `width_tiles` 2 and 2, `SOCKET_CLASS` 1 and 1, lane multisets equal, no `GEOM_OVERLAP` under Layout's `rects_in` test: the home `spine_corridor` east hull wall is x [672, 696) per Derelict Authoring D.13); B is docked at `frame_shift_px = (696, 384)`: `|Pairs| = 1`, offer = 1, the prompt shows. The same stance with B still 24 px short of its dock (`world(b) - world(a) = (720, 384)`): `docked` is false, `|Pairs| = 0`, offer = 0, **no prompt and no "can't weld" icon**.
588	
589	The seam_cut_offer formula is defined as:
590	
591	`seam_cut_offer(seat, s) = ( tool_in_hand(seat) == tool_cutter ) AND lit(seat, s) AND in_reach(seat, s) AND ( socket_state(s) == WELDED ) AND ( seam_state(seam_of(s)) == ACTIVE ) AND ( foot_section(seat) IN keep_sections(seam_of(s)) )`
592	
593	Derived: `keep_sections` is the component of the weld forest that keeps its `body_id` (the one containing the body's `origin_section_id`, LY-17; in MVP the home-ship side), from Layout's `detach_preview` (ASK L1). There is deliberately **no `CUT_BLOCKED` term**: the prompt is offered, `CUT_BLOCKED` is checked at begin, handoff and completion (D.13), and the clean hatch-presence oracle stays a rejection the player can see (MSA-21).
594	
595	**Variables:**
596	
597	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
598	|---|---|---|---|---|
599	| `tool_in_hand(seat)` | enum | tool class id | Suit (`tool_cutter`, class {8}, slot 1) | The equipped tool |
600	| `lit`, `in_reach` | bool | 0 or 1 | as above | |
601	| `socket_state(s)` | enum | as above | Layout | Must be `WELDED` |
602	| `seam_of(s)` | seam id | `seam_id` allocated by the Graph | Layout `welds[]` | The seam the socket is part of |
603	| `seam_state` | enum | `ACTIVE`, `CUT` | Layout / Graph | Only an `ACTIVE` seam can be cut |
604	| `foot_section(seat)` | section id | a section of the seat's body | Body `BDY D.10` | The section containing the seat's foot **origin** (BDY-23) |
605	| `keep_sections(seam)` | set of section ids | 1..`MAX_SECTIONS` | Layout `detach_preview` (ASK L1) | Sections that keep `body_id` after the cut |
606	
607	**Output Range:** boolean. **Example:** welded pair, seat standing in the home-ship airlock (a section in the home component): offer = 1. The same seat standing in derelict B's `b_dock`: `foot_section` is in the leaving component, offer = 0 and **no cut prompt exists on the derelict side** (the self-strand trap is unreachable). A `FREE` socket: offer = 0 (state must be `WELDED`); a `CAPPED` socket: offer = 0 (terminal).
608	
609	### D.3 Host and mate selection
610	
611	The host_and_mate formula is defined as:
612	
613	`host_of(a, b) = ( kind(sec(a)) == HOME AND kind(sec(b)) == DERELICT )` ; `(socket_a, socket_b) = argmin over Pairs(s) of ( socket_key_a , socket_key_b )` in that lexicographic order, with `Pairs(s)` as in D.2; the pair is empty when `Pairs(s)` is empty *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the section variable is renamed `sec` so `s` means only a socket; the focused socket seeds `Pairs(s)`; and the tie-break over candidate pairs is stated)*
614	
615	Derived: if both sections are DERELICT `[VS]`, `host_of` instead holds for the ordering whose `socket_a` is on the body with the lower `body_id`. **When the HOME section has several sockets** `[VS]`, a seat focusing a derelict socket `s` has one candidate pair per FREE HOME socket that passes `can_attach` and `docked`, and the pair with the lowest `socket_key_a` wins, then the lowest `socket_key_b`; a seat focusing a HOME socket has `socket_a = s` and the tie-break runs over the mates. In the MVP there is one pair, so no tie-break fires. The seat may stand on either side and focus either socket; Assembly derives the ordered pair, so the surviving body is always the home-ship's and the absorbed derelict body is re-based (LY-16 / LY Open Question 21: confirmed).
616	
617	**Variables:**
618	
619	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
620	|---|---|---|---|---|
621	| `kind(s)` | enum | `HOME`, `DERELICT` | Graph LS-17 | Section kind |
622	| `body_id` | int | 0..`MAX_BODIES` - 1 | Layout | The tie-break for a two-derelict pair `[VS]` |
623	| `socket_key` | string id | stable, ordered by byte comparison | Layout | The tie-break among several candidate pairs `[VS]` |
624	| `sec(x)` | section id | a section of the loaded set | Layout | The section a socket belongs to *(renamed from the reused `s`, re-review)* |
625	| `Pairs(s)` | set | as D.2 | calculated | Candidate ordered pairs containing the focused socket |
626	
627	**Output Range:** one ordered pair `(socket_a, socket_b)` or the empty pair (no offer). Deterministic: the same state always selects the same pair, which replay and MIRROR rely on. **Example:** the seat stands in derelict B's `b_dock` and focuses `sock_b_w`; `kind(derelict_b)` is DERELICT, `kind(home_ship)` is HOME; the pair is `(sock_airlock_e, sock_b_w)` regardless of which socket was focused, and B is the absorbed side.
628	
629	### D.4 Seam properties at weld (cited from the Graph, worked at MVP values)
630	
631	The seam_at_weld formula is defined as:
632	
633	`plan_seam = seam_at_weld( q , cap_a , cap_b , L_seam )`; **owned by the Graph (`LSG D.14`, registry `seam_at_weld`; `LSG D.2` for `A_seam_m`); Assembly supplies `q` (D.1) and the plan's `L_seam`, restates no expression and adds no term**
634	
635	**Variables:**
636	
637	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
638	|---|---|---|---|---|
639	| `q` | int (permille) | `Q_MIN` to 990 (D.1) | D.1 | Supplied by Assembly |
640	| `L_seam` | int (tiles) | 1-12 | Layout `width_tiles`, via `socket_plan` | MVP value 2 |
641	| `cap_a`, `cap_b` | int (loop units per step) | per port | the two joined ports' `cap` (Item DB defs; authored for bare nodes) | POWER lane: `mod_breaker_junction` CABLE ports, 3000 each (Item DB def 12, AC-79). O2 lane: `dj_air` and `dj_b_dock` are bare DUCT_JUNCTION nodes whose `cap` no design file publishes: **GAP, symbol `cap_duct`, `[UNV]`**, ASK G6(d) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: still unpublished after three routings with no owner (Item DB Open Question 30, Graph open-question row 26, OQ-DA-33). The only O2-lane value that depends on it is `cap_seam`; `hp_seam`, `leak_bp` and `A_seam_m` do not, and are worked below. Proposed working value for the owner to confirm or replace: `cap_duct` = 1200 mGU/step, equal to the largest O2-lane port in the Item DB (`mod_o2_tank`, retuned cap 1200), so the junction is never the bottleneck of the lane it joins. It is a proposal, not a fact, and no assertion rests on it until the owner publishes the value and the registry carries it as `cap_duct_junction`.)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: **owner assigned: Derelict Authoring**, which authors the bare DUCT_JUNCTION nodes `dj_air` and `dj_b_dock` (DA-19). It is asked to publish `cap_duct_junction` in the registry; the proposed 1200 mGU/step is acceptable as the first value `[PLACEHOLDER]`. Severity: the creative-director rules this RECOMMENDED, because implementation starts on the injected value; the owner must be assigned before the O2-weld Integration story starts, and it is (routed as a hard requirement in T13).)* |
642	| `A_SEAM_MAX`, `SEAM_LEAK_INITIAL_BP`, `SEAM_WEARIN_BP_PER_100`, `WELD_DP_WARN`, `LEAK_HP` | int | 16, 10000, 100, 300 dkPa, 4000 | Graph tuning (cited, locked) | Used only inside the Graph's expressions |
643	
644	**Output Range:** the Graph's own: `cap_seam` 700 to 995 permille of the lesser port across Assembly's `q` range, `hp_seam` 4000 to 9900, `leak_bp` starts at 10000, `A_seam_m` per `LSG D.2`.

646	**Example (MVP POWER lane, `q` 850):** `cap_a = cap_b = 3000`; `cap_seam = floor(3000 x 925 / 1000) = 2775 W`; `hp_seam = 8500` (above `HP_OK` 7000 and `LEAK_HP` 4000); `leak_bp = 10000`; `A_seam_m` = 720 milli flow units at period 0 (the Graph's value, LSG D.2: 360 per tile over 2 tiles), 360 at period 50 and 0 at period 100 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. The O2 lane: `cap_seam = floor( min(cap_duct_a, cap_duct_b) x 925 / 1000 )`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: completed as far as the data allows. **O2 lane at `q` 850, `L_seam` 2:** `hp_seam` = 8500, `leak_bp` = 10000 and `A_seam_m` = 720 at period 0, all independent of the duct port cap and identical to the POWER lane, because `A_seam_m` depends only on `q`, `L_seam` and `leak_bp` (`LSG D.2`); **verified against LSG D.14 (2026-10-27):** `hp_seam = q x 10`, `leak_bp = SEAM_LEAK_INITIAL_BP` and `A_seam_m` per D.2 are computed per seam from `q`, `L_seam` and `leak_bp`, and only `cap_seam = floor(min(cap_a, cap_b) x (500 + q/2) / 1000)` reads the ports' caps. `cap_seam` is `floor(min(cap_duct_a, cap_duct_b) x 925 / 1000)`: with the proposed `cap_duct` 1200 `[UNV]` it would be `floor(1200 x 925 / 1000)` = 1110 mGU/step; with a hypothetical 800 it would be 740; the AC asserts the formula with the injected value, and asserts the number only once the owner publishes `cap_duct`. The O2 half of the weld Integration story is the only work gated on this: the kernel, the PROJECTOR (S3), the fault model (S6) and the power-lane weld proceed.)* Wear-in (cited): `leak_bp` falls 100 bp per 10 s period from 10000, so the weep tapers linearly (720, 360 and 0 milli at periods 0, 50 and 100 for `q` 850) and stops at period 100: `100 x 10 s = 1000 s`, about 16.7 minutes; at `q` 990 it is 2 milli until `leak_bp` falls below 6250 (period 38, about 6.3 minutes) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. Surge (cited, `LSG D.14`): home bay at 1000 dkPa against a derelict room at 150 dkPa gives `|dP|` = 850 > `WELD_DP_WARN` 300, so `surge[].warn` is true and the closed hatch creaks (`SEAL_STRAIN`); the weld is permitted and moves nothing. Assembly's cue reads `warn` as a boolean only (MSA-15).
647	
648	### D.5 Weld offset prediction and the actor invariant
649	
650	The frame_shift_prediction_equal formula is defined as:
651	
652	`frame_shift_px = offset_a + pos_a - pos_b - offset_b_old` ; the apply asserts `LM2.frame_shift_px == predicted` (else `MSA_SHIFT_DRIFT`) ; `docked(a, b, fs) = ( vel(a) == vel(b) ) AND ( world(b) - world(a) == fs )` ; `abs(actor) = world(body) + pos_curr`
653	
654	Derived: the first is Layout's `LY D.6` (attach), the third Body's `BDY D.8`; Assembly computes nothing new, it compares the value predicted in `validate` (V3) with the value LM2 returns (A3) and BM3 consumes (A4). Because `offset_a`, `pos_a` and `pos_b` all lie on the 24-px grid (`GRID_24` lint), so does the result (the 24-grid closure, `LY D.6`).
655	
656	**Variables:**
657	
658	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
659	|---|---|---|---|---|
660	| `offset_a`, `offset_b_old` | int pair (px) | on the 24-px grid; `(0, 0)` for a freshly built single-section body (LY-25) | Layout | Host section offset in the surviving body; absorbed section offset in its own body |
661	| `pos_a`, `pos_b` | int pair (px) | on the 24-px grid, local >= 0 | Layout socket reference points: `(line_px, start_px)` for facing E or W | The two sockets' reference points |
662	| `frame_shift_px` | int pair (px) | on the 24-px grid, far below `WORLD_COORD_LIMIT` 2^22 | calculated (Layout) | The absorbed body's frame origin in the host frame; every absorbed section GAINS it |
663	| `world(a)`, `world(b)`, `vel(a)`, `vel(b)` | int pairs | Body ranges | `body.state` | Exterior poses and velocities |
664	| `pos_curr` | int pair (px) | in the actor's body frame | `body.state` | The actor's position |
665	
666	**Output Range:** exact integers. `delta_abs = frame_shift_px - (world(b) - world(a))` is `(0, 0)` iff the position half of `docked` holds; when it does not hold the weld still succeeds in the simulation and the absorbed hull jumps by `delta_abs` in the exterior layer only (reachable only in the residual window of E-17; the camera cut does not hide it, BDY-27, and the former fallback of dropping the `docked` term is deleted) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.
667	
668	**Example (DA-10):** `offset_a = (0, 0)`, `pos_a = (720, 672)`, `pos_b = (24, 288)`, `offset_b_old = (0, 0)`: `frame_shift_px = (0 + 720 - 24 - 0, 0 + 672 - 288 - 0) = (696, 384)` (29 x 24 and 16 x 24). With `world(home) = (1000, 500)` and `world(B) = (1696, 884)`, equal velocity: `world(b) - world(a) = (696, 384)`, docked, `delta_abs = (0, 0)`. An actor on B at `pos_curr = (100, 300)` has `abs = (1696, 884) + (100, 300) = (1796, 1184)` before; BM3 gives `pos_curr = (796, 684)` in the host frame, `abs = (1000, 500) + (796, 684) = (1796, 1184)`: equal. Not docked (`world(B) = (1720, 884)`): the difference is `(720, 384)`, `delta_abs = (696, 384) - (720, 384) = (-24, 0)`, the case the offer gate keeps away from the player. (Layout's own `LY D.6` example, `(576, 96)`, is a different socket placement and is not the MVP pair.) A weld followed by a cut of the same seam returns `pos_curr -= frame_shift_px` and zeroes the sub-pixel part, so it is **not** an identity on `pos_curr`; tests assert `abs` and section-local position.
669	
670	### D.6 Cut mode
671	
672	The cut_mode formula is defined as:
673	
674	`cut_mode(seam) = SEALED if ( for all o in openings(seam): area(o) == 0 ) AND ( for all e in fluid_sub_edges(seam): valve(e) == CLOSED ) AND ( for all c in cable_sub_edges(seam): breaker(c) == OPEN ), else RAGGED`
675	
676	Derived: the three clauses are exactly the as-welded state `weld_join` leaves (`LSG D.14`: opening `area` 0, valves CLOSED, breaker OPEN). The test reads **positions only**, never `hp`, `state` or `served_pm`. It is evaluated once, in the completion `apply` (step A1), and the single result is passed identically to M3 and LM3. No payload, prompt or cue carries or names a mode.
677	
678	**Variables:**
679	
680	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
681	|---|---|---|---|---|
682	| `area(o)` | int | 0..`area_max` | Graph via `seam_view` (ASK G3) | Opening area (the hatch) |
683	| `valve(e)` | enum | `OPEN`, `CLOSED` | Graph via `seam_view` | PIPE and DUCT sub-edge valve position |
684	| `breaker(c)` | enum | `OPEN`, `CLOSED` | Graph via `seam_view` | CABLE sub-edge breaker position |
685	| `cut_mode` | enum | `SEALED`, `RAGGED` | calculated | The `boundary_mode` for M3 and LM3 |
686	
687	**Output Range:** two values, deterministic. SEALED: nothing leaks, the socket becomes `CAPPED`, tombstones with a cap plate. RAGGED: per former opening a virtual hole `A_CUT` 24 on each side as a hull stub of `hp` 2500 (severity 4 BREACH, EXOGENOUS, exempt from the fairness gate, LS-16), each fluid port an `open_end` leaking at `OPEN_END_RATE_PM` 500 until `cap_port`; a 20-tile room reaches the DECOMP band in 382 steps (38 s) and VACUUM in 960 steps (96 s) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; the socket becomes `CUT_OPEN`. All cited from the Graph.
688	
689	**Example (MVP seam: one hatch OPENING, one O2 DUCT sub-edge, one POWER CABLE sub-edge):**
690	
691	| hatch `area` | O2 valve | breaker | `cut_mode` | what the player saw beforehand |
692	|---|---|---|---|---|
693	| 0 | CLOSED | OPEN | SEALED | a quiet seam: no creak, no frost, no valve hiss, no draught *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the bead's own weep hiss may still be present during wear-in and says nothing about the mode, MSA-23 item 1)* |
694	| 64 (open) | CLOSED | OPEN | RAGGED | the leaf standing open with a draught across the threshold |
695	| 0 | OPEN | OPEN | RAGGED | a hiss at the open valve's lane |
696	| 0 | CLOSED | CLOSED | RAGGED | the junction's own powered state |
697	| 64 | OPEN | CLOSED | RAGGED | all three |
698	| 0 | OPEN | CLOSED | RAGGED | the open valve's hiss and the junction's powered state *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
699	| 64 | CLOSED | CLOSED | RAGGED | the open leaf with a draught and the junction's powered state *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
700	| 64 | OPEN | OPEN | RAGGED | the open leaf with a draught and the open valve's hiss *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
701	
702	*(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the matrix is now all eight combinations of hatch, valve and breaker. Two quantifier cases follow from the formula and are tested with it: a hatch at `area` 1 (partly open) is RAGGED because only `area` 0 satisfies the first clause, and a seam with two openings is SEALED only if **both** are 0, so one at `area` 0 and one at `area` 1 is RAGGED.)*
703	
704	A hatch closed but a hallucinated "closed" valve that is truly open: RAGGED; the hiss is the consequence-channel witness the player could have heard (MSA-23). A hatch opened during a cancelled-and-resumed cut makes the resumed cut RAGGED because the mode is re-derived at completion.
705	
706	### D.7 Channel timing and exposure
707	
708	The channel_timing formula is defined as:
709	
710	`T_done = Tb + D - resume_offset` ; `T_apply = T_done + 1` ; `blocks = D / GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` ; `exposure_s = ( D - resume_offset ) / TICK_RATE` ; `tool_pushes = D - resume_offset` ; constraint `D mod GRAPH_STEP_TICKS == 0`
711	
712	Derived: the clock, the abort set, the ledger and the noise are Interaction's (IA-14, IA-16, IA-33); Assembly supplies only `D` and consumes `T_done`. Accrual is at `e = T - Tb` = 1 to `D - resume_offset`, so the DONE handoff is the P3 of tick `T_done` and the completion applies in the P2 of `T_apply` (MSA-3). `resume_offset = blocks_done x B` while the ledger entry is valid (`T - abort_tick <= PARTIAL_TTL_TICKS`), else 0 (`IA D.6`, cited). A cancel wastes at most `B - 1` accrued ticks (the partial block is not credited), so cancel-to-peek is never free. **Minimum resumed channel** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: `D - resume_offset` can be as small as `B` = 6 ticks (one Graph block left), which is why the BUSY gate of D.11, not a channel-length floor, guards the handoff.
713	
714	**Variables:**
715	
716	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
717	|---|---|---|---|---|
718	| `Tb` | int64 tick | >= 0 | the P2 tick of `begin_*` | Begin tick (held as two 32-bit integers or a string at the serialisation boundary, SL-2) |
719	| `D` | int ticks | 240-480, multiple of 6 | `WELD_CHANNEL_TICKS` 360 / `SECTION_CUT_CHANNEL_TICKS` 240 `[PLACEHOLDER]` | Declared duration |
720	| `resume_offset` | int ticks | 0..`D - B` | Interaction ledger (cited) | Credited ticks from an earlier aborted channel |
721	| `B` = `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` | int | 6 | Graph (cited) | Block length |
722	| `TICK_RATE` | int | 60 | Kernel (cited) | Ticks per second |
723	| `PARTIAL_TTL_TICKS` | int | 600 | Interaction (cited) | Ledger lifetime |
724	
725	**Output Range:** `blocks` 40 to 80; exposure 4.0 s (cut) to 8.0 s (weld at 480) fresh; `T_apply - Tb = D + 1` for a fresh channel. The floor 240 keeps both channels in the LONG bar class (`BAR_LONG_FROM_TICKS` 240); the ceiling 480 is set by analogy with IA I-9, not a lock on Assembly.
726	
727	**Example:** a fresh weld begins in P2 of `Tb` = 437039: `D` 360, `blocks` 60, accrual on ticks 437040..437399, `T_done` 437399, `T_apply` 437400; 360 TOOL pushes, exposure 6.0 s, **no** LOUD at the completion. A fresh seam cut begins at `Tb` = 439759: `D` 240, `T_done` 439999, `T_apply` 440000, 240 TOOL pushes and one LOUD at DONE (pushed by Interaction), exposure 4.0 s. A weld cancelled by movement at `e` = 100 credits block 16 (`resume_offset` 96); a re-begin within 600 ticks has remaining `360 - 96` = 264 ticks (4.4 s), so the total accrued TOOL ticks are 99 + 264 = 363, three more than the fresh 360 (the wasted partial block).
728	
729	### D.8 Body-count bound
730	
731	The bodies_after_worst_sequence formula is defined as:
732	
733	`N(t) = N0 - W(t) + C(t)` with `C(t) <= W(t)`, therefore `N(t) <= N0` for every reachable sequence; `bodies_after_worst_sequence = N0`; lint `N0 <= min( MAX_BODIES , BODIES_LIVE_MAX )`
734	
735	Derived: a weld merges two bodies into one (the absorbed body is `DISSOLVED`), a cut splits one into two, and every cut needs a prior `ACTIVE` weld, so cuts never outnumber welds. Sockets are terminal (LY-13), so `W <= P`, the number of authored socket pairs. Assembly adds no capacity rule; `can_detach`'s `CAPACITY` reason and a `MAX_SECTIONS_PER_BODY` value are deferred to Vertical Slice (Layout Open Question 8).
736	
737	**Variables:**
738	
739	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
740	|---|---|---|---|---|
741	| `N0` | int | 1..`MAX_BODIES` | built at load (Web Map `init_world`, Layout) | Live bodies before any Assembly command |
742	| `W(t)`, `C(t)` | int | 0..`P`; 0..`W(t)` | count of Layout `welds[]` rows ever welded / ever cut | Welds and cuts applied by tick `t` |
743	| `P` | int | MVP 1 | authored socket pairs | Possible welds |
744	| `MAX_BODIES` | int | 8 | Layout (cited, locked) | Hard cap |
745	| `BODIES_LIVE_MAX` | int | 4 `[PLACEHOLDER]` | 2D Lighting (cited) | Cross-body lighting cap |
746	
747	**Output Range:** MVP `N(t)` is 4 before the weld, 3 after it, 4 after the one cut. **Zero margin:** the worst case equals `BODIES_LIVE_MAX` exactly. Any body added outside Assembly (a second pod, a loose piece Web Map keeps alive) or any Vertical Slice socket-economy change exceeds it, which degrades cross-body lighting (stand-ins) without breaking the sim (MSA-41, ASK LT1). **Example:** home + A + B + pod = 4; weld (B dissolves into home): `4 - 1 + 0` = 3; cut: `4 - 1 + 1` = 4; a second weld attempt returns `SOCKET_NOT_FREE`, so `N` stays 4 and `4 <= min(8, 4)` holds with margin 0.

**What the surfaces read (and nothing else).** The HUD reads `focus_view` and `channel_view` (Interaction's IA-41 views); the presenters read the local seat's `last_result` from `assembly.state` (a SIM block, replicated as `SHARED_SUMMARY`) and `welds[]`-derived geometry from Layout. Neither reads `pending`, any Graph node or edge, `forced_mode`, `served_pm` or any `PERCEPTION_OUT` block. Assembly publishes two pure predicates for the surfaces (`weld_offer` and `seam_cut_offer`, used as the `eligible` of the `begin_*` declaration rows, MSA-12) and the pure read `last_shape_change_T()` for Save/Load; it publishes no other read view *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: except `ragged_breach_open()`, the pure read Save/Load consults to withhold the `ASSEMBLY_CUT` event while the keep-side cut room is venting or a keep-side port is uncapped, MSA-33)*.
====
**MSA-18 — The seam cut is offered only from the component that keeps its body.** *Rule:* `seam_cut_offer(seat, socket)` (formula D.2) is true iff the cutter is the equipped tool, the seat is `lit` and `in_reach` of a `WELD_SOCKET` subject whose socket is `WELDED` on an `ACTIVE` seam, **and the seat's foot-origin section lies in the component that keeps its `body_id`** (the component containing the body's `origin_section_id`, Layout LY-17; in MVP the home-ship side). On the derelict side of a welded seam no cut prompt exists. This is a geometry-plus-own-position read, so it is IMMEDIATE and P4-safe; the begin-time backstop is the existing reason `NOT_ELIGIBLE`, deliberately **not** `CUT_BLOCKED`, which stays the clean "a human is in the passage" oracle (MSA-21). It needs a Layout read: ASK L1, a pure `detach_preview(seam_id) -> {keep_sections[], leave_sections[], moved_sections[], frame_shift_px, rects[]}` computing the same components as LM3 and `LY D.12` without mutating (if refused, Assembly would derive components itself from `welds[]`, a duplicate of Layout logic that is not recommended). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: **answered**; Layout publishes `detach_preview` in its read table (Layout 1.5 (read table), "the same components and re-base as LM3 / D.12 computed without mutation") and lists it in its Assembly row. ASK L1 is closed.)* *Why:* body transfer follows the actor's foot origin (BDY-23). A player who cuts from the derelict side ends alone on a new, sealed, drifting body with no free socket (both are terminal) and no pod: an unrecoverable, untelegraphed trap whose only recovery path (Web Map & Transit) is out of MVP scope (WM-23: stranded-crew recovery deferred to Vertical Slice A / B). A trap fails "no lie is unfalsifiable" and the flow principle that the cost of a failure be proportional to its frequency. *Cost:* the player cannot abandon the home-ship and keep the derelict; that play is deferred to Vertical Slice design with a Web Map recovery path (Open Question 3; Default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20): D57) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. *(orchestrator ruling: adopts the systems-designer's keep-side rule and the game-designer's G6 option A; **rejects** the systems-designer's second clause, "no cut while anyone is on the leaving piece", as a **blanket gate** for MVP and Vertical Slice A. It is a far-side crewmate gate, which the game-designer's G8 and the binding decision "death is a bitch; it happens" exclude for those builds, and in solo play it is vacuous. The creative-director's `CUT_STRANDS` proposal is **adopted by default for Vertical Slice B by user ruling D53** (below) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. CD-GDD-ALIGN revision 2026-10-26: the ruling stands, but it is no longer written as an unqualified "there is no gate"; the victim's counterplay is a rule of this section and the Vertical Slice B outcome is tied to a recovery path.)*

**The victim's counterplay (rule, CD-GDD-ALIGN) `[VS-B]`.** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the whole paragraph needs a crewmate on the leaving piece, so it is co-op, is not in the MVP and gates nothing in the MVP. The `CUT_BLOCKED` reject itself, the hatch-cap hazard of Body BDY-24, is an MVP rule and is exercised in the MVP with a Body double (AC-MSA-36); only the far-side crewmate's use of it as a veto is `[VS-B]`.)* A keep-side cut can leave a crewmate on the leaving piece, so the victim is given a way to refuse it, using only rules this GDD already owns. 771	### D.10 CASCADE deferral deadline `[VS]`
772	
773	The cascade_defer_deadline formula is defined as:
774	
775	`deadline_T = first_deferred_T + CASCADE_CUT_DEFER_MAX_TICKS` ; at each tick `T`: if `actors_overlapping(rects)` is empty then APPLY, else if `T >= deadline_T` then ABANDON, else DEFER
776	
777	Derived: `seam_cut {cause CASCADE}` is specified and tested through a stub submitter; no MVP system submits one (MSA-22). It is preceded by the P2 tell window and by the Graph's `W_MIN_WARNING_S` 10 s gate (ENDOGENOUS transitions only), and **abandons, never forces**, on expiry (BDY-24).
778	
779	**Variables:**
780	
781	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
782	|---|---|---|---|---|
783	| `first_deferred_T` | int64 tick | | `assembly.state.cascade_deferred` (reserved, empty in MVP) | Tick of the first deferral |
784	| `CASCADE_CUT_DEFER_MAX_TICKS` | int ticks | 60-1800, multiple of 6 `[PLACEHOLDER]`, default 600 `[VS]` | data file (registry candidate ★) | Expiry |
785	| `W_MIN_WARNING_S` | int s | 10 | Graph (cited) | The fairness gate, a separate and independent knob |
786	
787	**Output Range:** three outcomes (apply, defer, abandon). The equality of 600 ticks with `W_MIN_WARNING_S` x `TICK_RATE` (10 s x 60) is a coincidence of values, not a contract; no lint ties them. **Example:** `first_deferred_T` = 1000, default 600, `deadline_T` = 1600: the crewmate leaves the rectangles at 1210, the cut applies at 1210 (if the 10 s warning has elapsed); a crewmate who stays through 1600 gets ABANDON at 1600, the seam stays welded, the cut never fires.
788	
789	### D.11 Pending TTL
790	
791	The pending_ttl_ok formula is defined as:
792	
793	`pending_ttl_ok = ( PENDING_TTL_TICKS >= ceil( QUEUE_CAPACITY / MAX_CMDS_PER_TICK ) ) AND ( PENDING_TTL_TICKS <= MAX_AGE_TICKS_ACTION - 1 )` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* ; `earliest_NOT_TAKEN_T = submit_T + PENDING_TTL_TICKS + 1`
794	
795	Derived: the two clauses are, in order, the kernel's never-spuriously-stale invariant (`KRN D.7`: `max_age_ticks(any type) >= ceil(QUEUE_CAPACITY / MAX_CMDS_PER_TICK)`, a boot assertion) and Assembly's ceiling that a completion never outlives a begin's own age window. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the former third clause, `PENDING_TTL_TICKS + 1 < min(channels)`, is deleted. It was vacuous, because clause 2 caps the TTL at 119 and the channel floor is 240, and its premise was false under `resume_offset`: a resumed channel can be as short as one Graph block, 6 ticks (D.7), so "the next DONE is at least one whole channel after the next begin" does not hold. **The single guarantee that a new handoff never meets an unresolved `pending` is the `pending.kind != NONE` BUSY gate at site 1** (MSA-7): a `begin_*` is refused for as long as `pending` is set, so a new channel can only start after the TTL has resolved, whatever its length.)* Both completion types set `max_age_ticks = PENDING_TTL_TICKS`, so the kernel's `STALE` rejection and Assembly's `NOT_TAKEN` land in the same tick order: P2 rejects at `submit_T + PENDING_TTL_TICKS + 1`, then the P3 of that tick writes `NOT_TAKEN`. The result is that `DONE` and `NOT_TAKEN` are mutually exclusive (MSA-6).
796	
797	**Variables:**
798	
799	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
800	|---|---|---|---|---|
801	| `PENDING_TTL_TICKS` | int ticks | 8-119, default 12 `[PLACEHOLDER]` | data file (registry candidate ★) | Lifetime of a submitted completion |
802	| `QUEUE_CAPACITY` | int | 1024 | Kernel (cited, locked) | Command queue size |
803	| `MAX_CMDS_PER_TICK` | int | 128 | Kernel (cited, locked) | Dispatch cap per tick |
804	| `MAX_AGE_TICKS_ACTION` | int ticks | 120 | Kernel (cited, locked) | The age bound of an action command (a begin) |
805	| `submit_T` | int64 tick | | `assembly.state.pending.submit_T` | When `assembly.step` submitted the completion |
806	
807	**Output Range:** boolean at boot (a failing value fails the data lint); the default gives `earliest_NOT_TAKEN_T = submit_T + 13`, about 0.22 s after submission. **Example:** `PENDING_TTL_TICKS` 12: `12 >= ceil(1024/128)` = 8 yes; `12 <= 119` yes: valid. 7: fails the first clause (a legitimate completion held 8 ticks by queue truncation would be `STALE`). 119: valid, `earliest_NOT_TAKEN_T` = `submit_T + 120`. 240: fails the second clause (240 > 119) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. Under an injected backlog of 1 to 8 ticks the completion applies exactly once and `NOT_TAKEN` is never written.
808	
809	### D.12 Weld notification batch
810	
811	The weld_batch_key_budget formula is defined as:
812	
813	`keys_block = base_block + n_moved + n_actors + n_subject_deltas <= MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` ; checked per block, for each of `graph.state`, `layout.state`, `body.state`, `interaction.state`, `assembly.state`
814	
815	Derived: the kernel batches one notification per block (CR-10). The Graph's batch is fixed by its owner (`T`, `S/<seam_id>`, `SEC/<a>`, `SEC/<b>`, nothing else); Layout adds `SEC/` and `BODY/` keys for moved sections; Body adds pose and actor keys; Interaction adds only subjects whose registration changed (ASK I1(vii)). Exceeding `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` collapses a block's batch to `ALL` and costs a full rebuild, so the budget is checked, not assumed.
816	
817	**Variables:**
818	
819	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
820	|---|---|---|---|---|
821	| `base_block` | int | graph 4; layout 5; body 2; interaction 0; assembly 1 per seat that changed | the owners' key sets | Fixed keys |
822	| `n_moved` | int | MVP 1 (derelict B); worst case <= `MAX_SECTIONS` 24 | Layout | Sections whose offset changed |
823	| `n_actors` | int | 0..`MAX_ACTORS` 8 | Body | Actors transferred by BM3 or BM4 |
824	| `n_subject_deltas` | int | MVP <= 4 (door faces) | Interaction `sync_section` | Subjects whose registered state changed |
825	| `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` | int | 256 | Kernel (cited, locked) | Collapse threshold |
826	
827	**Output Range:** MVP weld: `graph.state` 4; `layout.state` <= 6 (the moved section's `SEC/` key coincides with `SEC/<b>`, so 5 is the likely union and 6 the bound); `body.state` <= 3 with one avatar (2 pose rows + 1 actor; <= 10 only at the `MAX_ACTORS` 8 cap); `interaction.state` <= 4; `assembly.state` <= 1 (one key per changed seat; only the welder's seat changes in an MVP weld). Worst case `layout.state` 5 + 24 = 29. All well under 256. **The one failure mode** is `sync_section` marking every subject of both sections (about 98 + 98 fixtures plus loose items and stubs, up to about 190 in the three-section case), which is why the ask is "mark only changed subjects". **Example:** home + B weld with one avatar on B: graph 4, layout 6, body 2 + 1 = 3, interaction 4, assembly 1: five batches, the largest 6 keys. Conservation and fresh-seam disconnection on the apply tick are asserted by the Graph itself (LS-24) and cross-checked by AC-MSA-25 and AC-MSA-67; they are not re-owned here.
828	
829	### D.13 Hatch-cap check (`CUT_BLOCKED`)
830	
831	The cut_blocked formula is defined as:
832	
833	`rects(seam) = { hatch_rect_a , hatch_rect_b }` with each of size `( WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH ) x ( width_tiles x TILE_PX )` in the body frame ; `cut_blocked = ( actors_overlapping( body_id , rects(seam) ) != empty )` with `ov( box , r ) = max(0, min(x1) - max(x0)) x max(0, min(y1) - max(y0)) > 0`
834	
835	Derived: `actors_overlapping` is Body's pure read (`BDY D.11`, cited); Assembly supplies the two rectangles from Layout's hatch geometry (LY-15) and the verdict handling: a `CHANNEL` cut rejects `MSA.CUT_BLOCKED` at begin, handoff and completion, a `CASCADE` cut defers (D.10). The list includes the cutter. The geometry guarantee that the cutter's own foot box can stand outside both rectangles within reach is a Layout and Authoring requirement (`SOCKET_STANCE_BAND_EMPTY`, ASK L2), not an Assembly term.
836	
837	**Variables:**
838	
839	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
840	|---|---|---|---|---|
841	| `WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH` | int (px) | 24 | art bible (registry `WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH`, value 24; Layout's hatch geometry consumes it) | Hatch plate depth |
842	| `TILE_PX` | int (px) | 48 | Pipeline (cited) | Tile size |
843	| `width_tiles` | int | 1-12; MVP 2 | Layout | Seam width: the plate is `width_tiles x 48` = 96 px long |
844	| `foot_box(a)` | half-open rect | 16 x 8 px (`FOOT_BOX_W` x `FOOT_BOX_H`) | Body `BDY D.2` | The actor's footprint at `pos_curr` |
845	| `REACH_PX` | int (px) | 72 | Controller (cited) | The interaction reach |
846	
847	**Output Range:** boolean; the list is in ascending `actor_id`. **Example (MVP pair, derived from DA-10 and `LY D.6`; rectangle coordinates are `[UNV]` until Layout publishes the hatch rectangles):** `rect_a` = `[696, 720) x [672, 768)` (the home airlock's east hull plate), `rect_b` = `[720, 744) x [672, 768)` (B's west hull plate after the weld). A crewmate at `pos = (700, 700)` has box `[692, 708) x [700, 708)`; overlap with `rect_a` is `(708 - 696) x 8 = 96 > 0`: blocked. A cutter standing at `pos = (680, 720)` has box `[672, 688) x [720, 728)`: no overlap with either rectangle (8 px of clearance, one foot-box half-width, the margin ASK L2 asks Layout to guarantee) and within `REACH_PX` 72 of the hatch face (16 px away): not blocked. One foot-box further east, `pos = (696, 720)`, box `[688, 704)`: overlap with `rect_a` is `8 x 8 = 64`, blocked; this is exactly what AC-MSA-37 probes.
848	
849	### D.14 Subject budget at the seam
850	
851	The subject_budget_at_seam formula is defined as:
852	
853	`S_total_after = S_total_before + n_subject_deltas` with the Interaction-owned lint `F + L_seed + C <= INTERACT_FIXTURE_BUDGET`, `P <= PLAYER_DROP_RESERVE`, `INTERACT_FIXTURE_BUDGET + PLAYER_DROP_RESERVE <= 144`, `S_total <= MAX_EXPOSURE_SUBJECTS`; **owned by Interaction (`IA D.10`, I-7); Assembly supplies only `n_subject_deltas` (door faces added or removed by the weld or cut)**
854	
855	**Variables:**
856	
857	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
858	|---|---|---|---|---|
859	| `n_subject_deltas` | int | weld: <= +4; cut: <= -4 plus stubs <= `C` | Interaction `sync_section` | Door faces registered by the weld; removed (and RAGGED stubs created) by the cut |
860	| `F`, `L_seed`, `C`, `P`, `A`, `H` | int | 0..120, 0..20, 0..18, 0..24, <= 4, <= 2 (`HORROR_SUBJECTS_MAX`) | Interaction (cited) | Fixtures, seeded loose items, cap stubs, player drops, actors, horrors |
861	| `INTERACT_FIXTURE_BUDGET`, `PLAYER_DROP_RESERVE` | int | 120, 24 | Interaction (cited) | The content lint |
862	| `MAX_EXPOSURE_SUBJECTS` | int | 192 | Emitter State (cited) | The hard cap |
863	
864	**Output Range:** a content lint, not runtime state. Over the hard cap a subject fails dark, which for a seam door reads as a hallucinated dead door (a P4 breach by accident). **Example (Interaction's registered figures, `legal_loaded_sets`):** S3 (home + B welded) `S_int` 113 + `P` 24 + `A` 4 + `H` 2 = 143, 49 below 192 *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; the seam's door faces are inside the registered S3 count. S4 `{home+B, A}`: `S_int` 145 + 30 = 175, 17 below 192 (every registered neighbourhood's `F + L_seed + C` is within `INTERACT_FIXTURE_BUDGET` 120) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)*. Which sections load is the decision of Web Map and Authoring, not the weld.
865	
866	### D.15 Apply budget split
867	
868	The apply_budget_split formula is defined as:
869	
870	`weld_apply_ms = m2 + lm2 + bm3 + 2 x sync + own + verifier_release <= MSA_WELD_APPLY_BUDGET_MS` ; `cut_apply_ms` has the same shape with `m3 + lm3 + bm4`; `install_apply_ms = check + m5 + release + clear + sync + own <= MSA_INSTALL_APPLY_BUDGET_MS`
871	
872	Derived: a documentation formula. The spike reports each term separately so that a failed budget points at an owner. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: **the 0.5 ms split is an allocation target, not a measurement, and it is optimistic for GDScript.** The example below implies well under a microsecond per synced subject (0.10 ms for two sections of roughly a hundred subjects each), which is native-code speed; an interpreted GDScript loop with dictionary access is plausibly 3 to 5 times slower, so a spike that fails 0.5 ms would be a false negative about the design. Rules: (1) a micro-benchmark S0 runs first and measures the per-call cost of a representative mutator, a `sync_section` over 100 subjects and the release verifier subset in GDScript on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK (R12), and the term budgets and `MSA_*_APPLY_BUDGET_MS` are **re-derived from S0** before S1 is judged; (2) the S1 fallback (splitting the apply across ticks behind a Graph-held "welding" state) triggers **only if the whole weld tick (P2 plus P3) exceeds `STEP_BUDGET_MS` 4**, the kernel's logging threshold, never merely because the 0.5 ms allocation is missed; (3) the per-term budgets stay as gating criteria on the named reference machines, pending spike measurement on RM-DESKTOP / RM-DECK (Open Question 6, closed by R12).)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R12)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the per-term budgets are **reported, not gated**; the one gate is the whole weld tick under `STEP_BUDGET_MS` 4 (AC-MSA-23). A re-derived budget is frozen by a committed change before the run that judges it, and is capped at 2.0 ms, the knob's safe-range ceiling, unless the user signs off a higher figure.)* The Graph's M2 alone is locked at <= 0.2 ms Release and sits inside the weld term.
873	
874	**Variables:**
875	
876	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
877	|---|---|---|---|---|
878	| `m2`, `m3`, `m5` | float ms | `m2` <= 0.2 (locked) | Graph | Mutator cost |
879	| `lm2`, `lm3` | float ms | allocation targets, `[UNV]` | Layout | Mutator cost |
880	| `bm3`, `bm4` | float ms | `[UNV]`; up to `MAX_ACTORS` 8 transfers | Body | Mutator cost |
881	| `sync` | float ms | `[UNV]` | Interaction `sync_section` | One section re-registration |
882	| `own` | float ms | `[UNV]` | `assembly.state` writes | Assembly's own work |
883	| `verifier_release` | float ms | <= 0.05 (INV-1, INV-2, INV-4, INV-5, INV-7; O(seams <= 48 + bodies <= 8 + actors <= 8)) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | Assembly | Release-build verifier subset (MSA-32) |
884	| `MSA_WELD_APPLY_BUDGET_MS`, `MSA_CUT_APPLY_BUDGET_MS`, `MSA_INSTALL_APPLY_BUDGET_MS` | float ms | 0.5, 0.5, 0.2 `[PLACEHOLDER]` | T9 | Budgets |
885	
886	**Output Range:** the sum must not exceed its budget, and the whole weld tick (P2 plus P3) stays under `STEP_BUDGET_MS` 4, a logging threshold and not a cut-off. **Example (allocation targets, not measurements):** `m2` 0.20 + `lm2` 0.05 + `bm3` 0.05 + `2 x sync` 0.10 + `own` 0.01 + `verifier_release` 0.05 = 0.46 ms <= 0.5. The P5 subscribers (PROJECTOR, Emitter, Lighting, Trail) are outside the apply and have their own budget (`MSA_WELD_FRAME_P5_BUDGET_MS` 8, PROJECTOR `PROJECTOR_WELD_BUDGET_MS` 4 `[UNV]`, no frame above `WELD_FRAME_HITCH_MAX_MS` 33).
887	
888	### D.16 Fault loss window
889	
890	The fault_loss_window formula is defined as:
891	
892	`fault_loss_ticks = T_fault - last_save_T` ; `fault_loss_ticks <= AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_TICKS + AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS` (10800 + 7200 = 18000 ticks, 5 minutes: the interval autosave is soft-gated, for example while `CHANNELLING` (SL-5), and a soft-blocked interval save may defer up to `AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS` 7200 before it is written anyway, so this sum is the ceiling); enabling the `ASSEMBLY_WELD` / `ASSEMBLY_CUT` events can only shorten the window, never lengthen it. The name is distinct from Save/Load's registered `loss_ticks` (`T_dead - T_g`, the death-rule loss), which measures a different quantity
893	
894	Derived: a defect inside an Assembly `apply` moves the kernel `RUNNING -> FAULTED` (CR-9), and the only exit is a player-initiated restore of the last autosave. This is the price of "no rollback" stated as a number so a reviewer can accept or reject it. It is **not** the death rule (SL-7); it shares only the loading path.
895	
896	**Variables:**
897	
898	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
899	|---|---|---|---|---|
900	| `AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_TICKS` | int ticks | 10800 | Save/Load (cited) | Interval autosave |
901	| `AUTOSAVE_MIN_GAP_TICKS` | int ticks | 1800 | Save/Load (cited) | Event coalescing floor (events can only add saves at least this far apart) |
902	| `AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS` | int ticks | 7200 | Save/Load (registry) | Longest wait of a soft-blocked interval save; after it the save is written anyway and tagged RISKY |
903	| `T_fault`, `last_save_T` | int64 ticks | | kernel; Save/Load | Tick of the defect; tick of the last autosave |
904	
905	**Output Range:** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the figures are relabelled. 10800 was called "typical" but it is a maximum: a defect lands uniformly inside the autosave interval, so the **mean** loss is about half of it.)* 0 to 18000 ticks (5 minutes of play) at the ceiling when a soft gate defers the interval save to `AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS`; **maximum 10800 ticks (3 minutes) and mean about 5400 ticks (1.5 minutes)** when no soft gate defers it; with events enabled the window shrinks toward the event save but is not computed here. **Example:** a defect in A3 of a weld 2 minutes (7200 ticks) after the last interval autosave: the player loses up to 7200 ticks of play, within the 10800 maximum and the 18000 ceiling (*Amended 2026-10-27 — design review:* the soft-gate fixture of AC-MSA-148 deliberately lands a fault at `fault_loss_ticks` = 17999, the largest value the formula allows, so the 18000 path is exercised and not only the 7200 case); the existing save file is never overwritten while FAULTED. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions) (D55): the window, mean about 5400, maximum 10800, ceiling 18000 ticks, is accepted. With the weld and cut event saves shipping in the MVP (D17) the window for a defect after a completed weld or cut shrinks toward the event save (the minimum gap is `AUTOSAVE_MIN_GAP_TICKS` 1800), and the RAGGED withhold and soft gate of MSA-33 cannot raise the ceiling because the soft gate is bounded by `AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS` 7200.)*
906	
907	### D.17 Outcome cue gate
908	
909	The outcome_cue_gate formula is defined as:
910	
911	`cue_plays(p) = ( p == local_seat ) AND ( last_result[p] != NONE ) AND ( ( p , last_result[p].T ) != last_seen ) AND ( T_now - last_result[p].T <= OUTCOME_CUE_WINDOW_TICKS )` ; `last_seen` is initialised on join and on restore to the `(p , last_result[p].T)` found at that moment *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the `last_result[p] != NONE` conjunct is evaluated first, so an empty `last_result` after a restore or a join is never subtracted from; without it the result depended on how GDScript treats the empty record and on evaluation order) (Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: keyed by `(PlayerId, T)`, local seat only, initialised on join and restore; the registry expression `cue_plays = (last_result.T != last_seen_T) AND (T_now - last_result.T <= OUTCOME_CUE_WINDOW_TICKS)` is superseded, see the registry request)*
912	
913	Derived: presentation consumes `last_result` once. `last_result` is runtime-only (MSA-4), so a restore leaves it empty and never replays a cue; a MIRROR join never plays a stale one **because `last_seen` is initialised to the value found at join** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*, not because of any clearing step: with `last_seen` unset the old formula would have played a result that was 30 ticks old at join. The outcome is presented by the verb family's one cue (MSA-34); the DONE outcome has its own completion cues (the bead locks, the burn-through).
914	
915	**Variables:**
916	
917	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
918	|---|---|---|---|---|
919	| `last_result[p].T` | int64 tick | >= 0 | `assembly.state` (runtime-only) | Presenter dedupe key, with `p` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
920	| `last_seen` | pair `(PlayerId, int64 tick)` | | presenter-local, not sim state | The last `(p, T)` the presenter acted on; initialised on join and restore *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
921	| `local_seat` | PlayerId | | the presenter's own seat binding | Cues play for the local seat only *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
922	| `T_now` | int64 tick | | kernel | Current tick |
923	| `OUTCOME_CUE_WINDOW_TICKS` | int ticks | 12-180, default 60 `[PLACEHOLDER]` | data file | Staleness bound |
924	
925	**Output Range:** boolean per presenter per `last_result` change. **Example:** a `NOT_TAKEN` is written at `last_result.T` = 437412; the presenter last saw 437000; the frame at 437420 has `T_now - last_result.T` = 8 <= 60: the cue plays once. A frame at 437500 after a hitch: 88 > 60, no cue (a stale cue after a hitch would read as a new failure). After a restore `last_result` is empty and no cue plays: the `!= NONE` conjunct is false and `T_now - last_result[p].T` is never evaluated *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. **Join example** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: a MIRROR client joins at tick 437442 and finds `last_result[1].T` = 437412 (30 ticks old, inside the 60-tick window); `last_seen` is initialised to `(1, 437412)`, so `cue_plays` is false and nothing plays; the next result at 437600 differs and plays once. A result of a crewmate (`p` = 2) never plays a cue on seat 1.
926	
927	### D.18 Welded-body capacity bounds
928	
929	The welded_body_capacity formula is defined as:
930	
931	`C_welded = sum over sections s in body of compartments(s) <= 12` (the Graph's LS-26 bound, read as the welded body, advisor R26) ; `nodes_loaded <= MAX_GRAPH_NODES` ; `edges_loaded + plan_edges <= MAX_GRAPH_EDGES`
932	
933	Derived: Assembly reads LS-26's "<= 12 compartments at the weld" as the **welded body's** compartment count (advisor R26). Whether LS-26 also bounds the loaded set `{home+B, A}` is the Graph's call (ASK G4). `CAPACITY` is a `can_join_static` reason; at MVP scale it is not at risk.
934	
935	**Variables:**
936	
937	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
938	|---|---|---|---|---|
939	| `compartments(s)` | int | per template | Layout / Authoring | Home 5, derelict A 4, derelict B 5 |
940	| `MAX_GRAPH_NODES`, `MAX_GRAPH_EDGES` | int | 4096, 8192 | Graph (cited, locked) | Capacity |
941	| `plan_edges` | int | MVP 3 (1 OPENING + 1 CABLE + 1 DUCT), provisional on the Graph's plan shape | `socket_plan` | Edges the weld adds (nothing else) |
942	
943	**Output Range:** boolean lint. **Example:** home 5 + B 5 = `C_welded` 10 <= 12; the loaded set including A is 14 (ASK G4). Graph load: about 105 nodes of 4096 and a few hundred edges of 8192 (the Graph's own estimate), plus 3 edges for the weld.

945	## Edge Cases
946	
947	Grouped by theme. Each case states the exact outcome and the rule that decides it. "Site 1/2/3" are the three call sites of the one predicate (MSA-7); "the sputter" is the weld family's one non-DONE cue and "the gutter" the cut family's (MSA-34). Ids `E-n` are stable references for the Acceptance Criteria.
948	
949	### Zero, maximum and out-of-range values
950	
951	- **E-1. If the data file ships `WELD_Q_DEFAULT` 1000 or 399**: the loader clamps it to 990 or 400 at load, raises `MSA_Q_CLAMPED` once, and every weld uses the clamped value (D.1). Playing on a q-1000 weld (or any q of 993 or more) would delete the weld's weep (the P1 tell) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; playing on a q-399 weld would leak at birth with no tell (a P2 break). The clamp runs at load, never per weld, so no weld can disagree with another.
952	- **E-2. If `WELD_CHANNEL_TICKS` or `SECTION_CUT_CHANNEL_TICKS` is not a multiple of `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` 6, or is outside 240-480**: the data lint fails at boot and the game does not start with that file (IA I-2 and the analogy to I-9). A channel that does not span whole Graph blocks would credit a partial block, and a duration below 240 would leave the LONG bar class.
953	- **E-3. If `PENDING_TTL_TICKS` is outside 8-119**: `pending_ttl_ok` (D.11) is false and the boot lint fails. Below 8 a legitimate completion held back by the kernel's per-tick truncation would be `STALE`; at 120 or above a completion could outlive a begin's own age window *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.
954	- **E-4. If a `plan` would take the welded body above 12 compartments or the Graph above `MAX_GRAPH_NODES` 4096 or `MAX_GRAPH_EDGES` 8192**: `can_join_static` returns `CAPACITY` at site 1 and the player gets the standard rejection cue (structural reasons are IMMEDIATE). The MVP welded body is 10 compartments and about 105 of 4096 nodes, so this is an authoring defect in MVP, not a play outcome (D.18).
955	- **E-5. If a `begin_*` is pressed while `assembly.state.pending.kind != NONE` for that seat**: it is rejected `BUSY` at site 1 and nothing is queued or opened. This BUSY gate is the single guarantee (D.11) that makes it impossible for a new handoff to meet an unresolved `pending`: the completion of the previous channel has either applied or resolved to `NOT_TAKEN` within 13 ticks, and the gate holds on a resumed begin too, whose channel can be as short as 6 ticks (D.7) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.
956	- **E-6. If the simulation runs with zero seats (a headless test, a menu state)**: `assembly.step` iterates an empty map, submits nothing and costs the idle budget only; `assembly.state` is `default_state()`. No Assembly path assumes a seat exists.
957	
958	### Simultaneous and ordering cases
959	
960	- **E-7 `[VS-B]` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. If two seats stand at the two different sockets of the one pair and both reach DONE on the same tick**: `assembly.step` submits two `weld` completions in ascending PlayerId order; the first applies; the second's `validate` fails `SOCKET_NOT_FREE` (both sockets are already `WELDED`), the command is Rejected, `pending` stays set and the second seat's outcome resolves as `NOT_TAKEN` at `submit_T + 13` with the weld sputter. Never a fault. The same socket cannot be contended at all: IA-34 gives the second seat `BUSY` at begin (one job per subject and verb class), so a double DONE needs the two *different* sockets (MSA-11 allows either to be focused); optional ASK I1(x) would close even that.
961	- **E-8 `[VS-B]` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. If the two seats' DONEs fall on consecutive ticks**: the second seat's handoff pre-check (site 2) sees the sockets `WELDED` and writes `REJECTED(SOCKET_NOT_FREE)`, submitting nothing, with the weld sputter. If the first completion is still queued (backlog), both completions are submitted and the first-queued applies, the other becomes `NOT_TAKEN` as in E-7. The welded state is single in every ordering (AC-MSA-59).
962	- **E-9. If a weld or cut applies in the same tick as a Graph hook tick (power `T mod 6 = 0`, atmo 2, failure 4)** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*: the apply runs in P2 and the due Graph hook in P3, so the first Graph hook that runs after the apply refreshes the topology (Graph phase 1 refresh at the head of any hook) and sees the bumped `topology_version` and the new seam; no half-state is observable. Assembly neither registers nor orders against the Graph's hooks.
963	- **E-10. If an earlier command in the same P2 queue changes the target (a crewmate's salvage completion removes `j_b_main`)**: P2 order is `(queued_tick, host_order)`, so the earlier command applies first; the weld's `validate` then sees the new state, and the full `can_join` in step A0 reads `PORT_ABSENT`. The result is `BLOCKED(PORT_ABSENT)`: both orderings are legal and deterministic.
964	- **E-11. If a breach opens in either section during the weld channel**: the channel does not abort (the abort set is closed, IA-15) and the weld still applies; the new seam opens with hatch area 0, so nothing crosses until the player opens the hatch, and the full `can_join` at apply step A0 reports the larger `surge[]` (no Assembly presenter reads it; the creak is the Graph's `SEAL_STRAIN` descriptor, VA-16), never a number. The player who wants to patch first simply moves: the ledger holds the progress for `PARTIAL_TTL_TICKS` 600.
965	- **E-12 `[VS-B]` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. If a crewmate stands on the absorbed (derelict B) side in an unrelated channel when a weld applies** (the single-player form is the welder's own case, E-56): BM3 transfers every actor on the absorbed body, which counts as a body transfer, so the Controller clears their `channel_ref` and Interaction aborts their channel with cause `BODY`, crediting any finished blocks (IA-14 row 1). No special case in Assembly; the welder on B sees no displacement when `docked` held.
966	- **E-13. If a crewmate (or any other actor, in the MVP a Body double) steps into a hatch rectangle during a seam-cut channel** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* (`[VS-B]` as co-op play; the double-based form gates the MVP, AC-MSA-36): the channel continues (a hazard is not an abort cause) and, at DONE, site 2 finds `actors_overlapping` non-empty and writes `REJECTED(CUT_BLOCKED)` with the gutter; the `LOUD` already went out at DONE, the seam stays welded and nothing is submitted. If the crewmate enters in the single tick between the handoff (P3 of `T_done`) and the completion (P2 of `T_apply`), site 3 rejects instead and the seat resolves as `NOT_TAKEN` 13 ticks after submission, with the same cue. "The ship will not close a seam on a crewmate" holds at all three sites.
967	- **E-14. If the cutter's own foot box overlaps a hatch rectangle**: the cut prompt is still offered (`seam_cut_offer` has no `CUT_BLOCKED` term, D.2) and begin is rejected `CUT_BLOCKED` with the standard rejection cue; stepping back out of the rectangle restores a valid begin. This is why Layout and Authoring must guarantee a legal stance at least one foot-box half-extent outside both rectangles within `REACH_PX` 72 (ASK L2, AC-MSA-37); without it the cut would be permanently self-blocked.
968	
969	### Target and state changes during the channel
970	
971	- **E-15. If the target lane node is salvaged before or during the weld channel (`j_main` or `j_b_main`, both def-backed; the bare `dj_*` nodes cannot be salvaged, DA-19)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: in MVP content this is meant to be unreachable, because ASK D2 authors the seam-lane node modules non-salvageable (MSA-8); the case stays specified for the Vertical Slice, for a defect and for the test fixture of AC-MSA-11: begin and the handoff pass (module-body state is never read there), the completion `validate` passes, and step A0 reads `PORT_ABSENT`: `last_result = BLOCKED(PORT_ABSENT)`, nothing else mutates, no `weld_join` call, the weld sputters. The cost is the six seconds; the world witness is the empty bay footprint at the lane node (LY-20), reachable within one walk.
972	- **E-16. If the weld is attempted onto a vacuum, frozen or dead section**: the weld is allowed and moves nothing (fresh seam: hatch area 0, valves closed, breaker open). The closed hatch creaks (`SEAL_STRAIN`) or frosts at the rim; the player decides when to open it. The weld is never refused for a hazard, only for structure (P1: the hazard is told by the hatch, not the prompt).
973	- **E-17. If `docked` stops holding during the 360-tick channel**: with Web Map & Transit's hold (ASK T1) this cannot happen. Without it, the handoff pre-check (site 2) re-tests `docked` and writes `REJECTED(NOT_DOCKED)` with the sputter, costing the six seconds. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the camera-cut fallback is deleted, Body's request accepted; the offer never drops the `docked` term.)* In the residual window between the site-2 re-test and the apply, a loss of `docked` still lets the weld apply (site 3 reads no pose) and the absorbed hull jumps by `delta_abs` in the exterior layer; Transit's hold (WM-22) makes that window unreachable, and the camera cut does not hide it (BDY-27). Site 3 deliberately does not re-test `docked` (BDY-27: weld legality takes no pose input).
974	- **E-18. If the target section is dormant (`SECTION_NOT_LOADED`)**: the prompt may still show (the offer reads no join structure) and begin is rejected with the standard rejection cue; no channel opens and no time is spent. Dormancy is a section flag, not module-body state, so it is IMMEDIATE.
975	- **E-19. If a weld is attempted while the seat carries a module**: no weld prompt exists (the carry lockout, PC-7 / IA-28, is Interaction's selector) and a forced `begin_weld` is `BUSY`. The player puts the module down or installs it; a torch needs two hands.
976	- **E-20. If the seam hatch is opened during a cancelled-and-resumed cut**: the ledger keeps the progress, but the mode is re-derived at completion, so the resumed cut is RAGGED (D.6). The open leaf and the draught are the witness; the player who wants a clean cut closes the hatch first.
977	- **E-21. If a RAGGED cut applies**: the Graph creates `A_CUT` 24 holes on both sides (including the home side), hull stubs `hp` 2500 and `open_end` ports; `sync_section` must create `stubs[]` entries for every uncapped `open_end` or the O2-lane port hiss could never be capped *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*, which would break P2 fairness (ASK I1(vii)). The cut is EXOGENOUS and player-caused, so it is exempt from `W_MIN_WARNING_S`; its tell was the world witnesses before the press. A 20-tile keep-side room falls to the DECOMP band in 382 steps (38 s) and to VACUUM in 960 steps (96 s) (LS-16, D.1) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. Capping a stub (V8's follow-up `begin_cap`, M12) stops that port's hiss only; it does not touch the hull hole. The hull hole has no subject in the MVP, so the player's answers are to leave and shut the door behind them (a closed OPENING isolates the room and the rest of the ship stops venting) or to accept the loss of the room until Vertical Slice content closes the hole.
978	- **E-22 `[VS-B]` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. If a keep-side cut leaves a crewmate on the leaving piece**: they are stranded on the detached body, which drifts without rotation. Counterplay (MSA-18): the 4 s lit, loud channel is the tell, and a crewmate who opens the hatch from the far side and stands in the passage before completion makes the cut `MSA.CUT_BLOCKED` (AC-MSA-123); a crewmate who only opens the hatch makes the cut RAGGED. If no one is in the passage the cut proceeds and there is no blanket far-side gate in MVP and Vertical Slice A (Q4: "death is a bitch; it happens"; in solo play a gate is vacuous). Recovery is Web Map & Transit's (ASK T1, ASK T2). Vertical Slice B gates it as `CUT_STRANDS` by default (user ruling D53): a keep-side cut with another seat in the leaving component is rejected `MSA.CUT_STRANDS` at handoff and completion unless the cutter's `harm_eligible` bit is set (MSA-18, Open Question 2) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.
979	- **E-53. If derelict B is welded into the home body** *(added after E-52 and kept last in this group; id kept stable for AC-MSA-122)*: the Graph's section record keeps `kind` DERELICT and so `rate_pm` 2000 (LS-17, LS-25: the rate is keyed on `kind`, and `weld_join`, LS-15, writes no section field). Endogenous wear and overload on B's nodes and edges therefore run at twice the home-ship rate after the weld. Every endogenous transition still passes the `W_MIN_WARNING_S` gate, so the tell is kept. Assembly writes no section field and adds no rule (MSA-2). Whether a graft keeps derelict compression is the Graph's call (ASK G7). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: **G7 is closed and 2x graft wear is confirmed as intended.** Graph LS-15 and LS-17 state that a welded section keeps its `kind` and `rate_pm` and that "a cut restores nothing"; Assembly keeps that: the graft is the ship's weak point, which is the motive to shed a worn graft (Player Fantasy, the cut anchor). **Observable in a session:** the Graph's own D.15 table gives, for a DERELICT section at `rate_pm` 2000, FUEL-DRIP at 5.3 minutes and HULL-FATIGUE at 6.2 minutes (against 10.5 and 12.5 at home), so an endogenous event on a grafted section is observable well inside a 30 to 60 minute session; AC-MSA-132 asserts the ratio on the Graph's fixtures.)*
980	
981	- **E-54. If the welder is swapped for another tool, or the seat is staggered or DOWNED, during a weld or cut channel** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; new)*: staggering and DOWNED end the channel with abort cause `BODY` (IA-15 lists "stagger, downed, body transfer, seat rebind" under `BODY`) and Interaction credits any finished blocks to the ledger; a tool swap makes `weld_offer` or `seam_cut_offer` false, so IA-14 row 6 aborts the channel with `NOT_ELIGIBLE` within `LIT_RECHECK_TICKS` 6 ticks (the `eligible` re-test of ASK I1(viii), answered). If neither fires before DONE (the swap lands in the last block), the handoff pre-check (site 2) finds `NO_TOOL` and writes `REJECTED(NO_TOOL)` with the family cue and submits nothing. A DOWNED seat never reaches DONE. No `pending`, no mutation. AC-MSA-135.
982	- **E-55 `[VS-B]`. 1595	## Acceptance Criteria
1596	
1597	*Ids AC-MSA-01 to AC-MSA-128 keep the pre-assigned meaning of the criterion index (T8) (AC-MSA-46 and AC-MSA-66 are absorbed into AC-MSA-01 and AC-MSA-58; split ids carry letters); the ids that the corrections and the Edge Cases added continue from AC-MSA-73 (AC-MSA-122 covers E-53; AC-MSA-123 to AC-MSA-128 were added by later revisions); ids 113 to 115 and 119, which the QA review had reserved, are reassigned to the Game Feel benchmarks. Every criterion carries a tag and a rule or edge-case reference. **Tags:** `(auto)` an automated test in `tests/unit/modular_ship_assembly/` or `tests/integration/modular_ship_assembly/`; `(lint)` a static scan or data lint; `(review)` a design or code review; `(manual)` a playtest or a retained screenshot in `production/qa/evidence/`; `(spike)` only the throwaway spike (see Spike Plan) can answer it. **Status markers:** `(depends: ASK Gn / CONFLICT Cn)` means the criterion rests on a provisional ask or an open conflict in the Dependencies tables (T14, T15); a failure there means "contract not yet agreed", not necessarily a defect. `[VS]` marks a Vertical Slice criterion whose rule is specified now. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: **`[VS-B]` marks a co-op criterion (it needs a second seat, a MIRROR client or a crewmate) and is excluded from the MVP gate**; where a rule has a double-based form that is single-player (for example `CUT_BLOCKED` with a Body double, AC-MSA-36), that form gates the MVP and says so. Ids AC-MSA-129 to AC-MSA-148 are added by the first design review; AC-MSA-05 is split into 05a and 05b.)**
1598	
1599	**Gate levels** (`.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`): Logic and Integration are BLOCKING; Visual/Feel and UI are BLOCKING and need a **retained** screenshot (a captured-and-discarded one is an assertion, not evidence); Config/Data is ADVISORY. Story typing: weld, cut, install and the verifier are Integration stories (several owners' mutators in one apply); D.1, D.6 to D.11, D.17 and D.18 are Logic; the knob and data lints are Config/Data; AC-MSA-68, 71, 113 and 114 are Visual/Feel plus UI.
1600	
1601	**Test rules.** Deterministic (no wall clock, no unseeded RNG, a fixed `world_seed`); isolated; assertions on `abs(actor)` and section-local position, never raw `pos_curr`; fixtures from constant files or factory functions; the doubles are a SYSTEM-origin submitter (tests cannot reach `weld` or `seam_cut` any other way), an Interaction double (except where a criterion says it needs the real one), a Body double with `docked` controllable, a Perception stub, and a Graph double for capacity. **Performance criteria are gated on the named reference machines** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R12)*: RM-DESKTOP (minimum-spec desktop: Windows 10/11 64-bit, 6-core/6-thread CPU of the Intel Core i5-9400F / AMD Ryzen 5 2600 class, 8 GB RAM, GPU of the GTX 1050 Ti 4 GB / RX 570 4 GB class, SATA SSD, 1920x1080 at 60 Hz, P99 CPU frame-time ceiling 16.6 ms) and RM-DECK (Steam Deck LCD 2022, SteamOS stable, 1280x800 at 60 Hz panel, 30 fps target, P99 ceiling 33.3 ms), recorded in `project.yaml` `qa.min_spec`; the build type for every wall-clock figure is a release export (Godot 4.7.2 release export template, not the editor and not a debug template), renderer `forward_plus`, vsync on, a 120-frame warm-up, with the startup read-back (renderer, driver) recorded with each result; a pass needs P99 <= 90 % of the machine's ceiling; the developer's machine is not a reference machine and its figures are indicative only; the measurement protocol is that release export build, 300 warm-up ticks discarded for the apply budgets, then the stated sample; apply budgets with headless render off, frame-time budgets with render on. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: **the performance criteria (AC-MSA-17b, 23, 62, 63, 108) stay gating**: the machines and build type are now named (R12, above), so a criterion is pending spike measurement on RM-DESKTOP / RM-DECK, not blocked, and the spike records the measured value as an input. A criterion marked `(spike)` produces a number for the spike report as a design input; the **story evidence** is the same assertion as an automated test under `tests/performance/modular_ship_assembly/` or `tests/unit/` run in the nightly job, never the throwaway spike report. The budgets themselves are re-derived from the S0 GDScript micro-benchmark before they are judged (D.15).)*
1602	
1603	**Lint harness** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: no harness was named, so the `(lint)` criteria could not run).* One script, `tools/lint/msa_lint.gd`, run as `godot --headless -s tools/lint/msa_lint.gd -- --rules all` from CI before the gdUnit4 suite; it scans the Assembly source folder (the code root's `modular_ship_assembly/` directory) and the data files under `assets/data/`, prints one line per finding as `LINT-MSA-<n> <file>:<line> <message>`, and exits non-zero on any finding. Each `(lint)` criterion names its rule: LINT-MSA-03 (AC-MSA-03: the only block written is `assembly.state`), LINT-MSA-06 (AC-MSA-06: no packed-array field), LINT-MSA-09 (AC-MSA-09: completion payload fields, `max_age_ticks`, TTL range), LINT-MSA-10 (AC-MSA-10: no second definition of the predicate; the equivalence itself is a unit test), LINT-MSA-13 (AC-MSA-13: no full `can_join`, `check_install_module` or node-state accessor in a PLAYER-origin `validate`), LINT-MSA-17 (AC-MSA-17a: `weld_offer` source), LINT-MSA-20 (AC-MSA-20 and 58: forbidden identifiers), LINT-MSA-30 (AC-MSA-30: calls Assembly never makes), LINT-MSA-47 (AC-MSA-47: no `push_stimulus`), LINT-MSA-57 (AC-MSA-57: no `PERCEPTION_OUT` reference), LINT-MSA-119 (AC-MSA-119: no shake, hit-stop, rumble or time-scale). The harness is a token and call-graph scan, so it can prove an absence ("this file never names X") and cannot prove an equivalence: **AC-MSA-10 ("identical bodies across three sites") is therefore not a lint.** It is made structural: the three call sites call **one shared function `_evaluate(site)`** (`weld_ready` and `seam_cut_ready` each have one), whose only per-site differences are the skips of T2a passed as an argument; AC-MSA-10 is an `(auto)` unit test with a recording double that proves all three sites reach that one function and that the first failing reason is the same at each, and the lint only asserts that no second implementation of the predicate exists.
1604	
1605	### Fixture and vocabulary block (referenced by the criteria as FB-n)
1606	
1607	**FB-1 MVP fixture constants.** Pair `sock_airlock_e` (home-ship, facing E, `line_px` 720, `start_px` 672) and `sock_b_w` (derelict B, facing W, `line_px` 24, `start_px` 288), `width_tiles` 2, lanes POWER 0 and O2 0, no COOLANT lane, offset `(696, 384)` (DA-10), `q` 850, cable port caps 3000 W, `L_seam` 2. Sections: home 5 compartments, B 5, A 4. Module fixtures: `mod_heater`, vacant hardpoint `hp_cargo_heater`; lane nodes `j_main` and `j_b_main` (def-backed, authored non-salvageable in MVP content, ASK D2; a salvageable stand-in exists only as a test fixture), `dj_air` and `dj_b_dock` (bare, DA-19, not salvageable) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. `REACH_PX` 72 (boundary rule as Interaction publishes it, inclusive or exclusive: cite IA, do not restate), `FOOT_BOX_W` 16, `FOOT_BOX_H` 8. Coordinates marked `[UNV]` in a criterion are recomputed from Layout's published hatch rectangles before the story starts.
1608	
1609	**FB-2 Command rows (T1).** `begin_weld`, `begin_seam_cut`, `install_module`: origin PLAYER, `OWNED_BY_ISSUER` (`actor_source body.state`, kernel CR-7) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*, coalesce NONE, `max_age_ticks` 120, modes CHANNEL, CHANNEL, TAP. `weld`, `seam_cut`: origin SYSTEM only, explicit `actor` field, coalesce NONE, `max_age_ticks` `PENDING_TTL_TICKS` 12, payload `{actor, socket_a, socket_b, cause}` and `{actor, seam_id, cause}` with `cause` CHANNEL (CASCADE for `seam_cut`, VS). I'm still unsure what detach_preview computes for an active seam since there's no definition of post-cut state—persisted layout shows welds and sections tied to body_id, but whether the keep side derives from the seam's pre-cut body isn't specified. This confirms the earlier finding MSA-33 remains unresolved.

One possible fix is to define the keep side after cutting as whichever section's body matches the body still holding the surviving origin_section, which would be a pure read of layout.state rather than relying on detach_preview. This exposes a real implementability gap: ragged_breach_open() gets evaluated while the seam is CUT, but detach_preview only applies pre-cut, meaning an implementer has to invent the derivation themselves—so I'm reconsidering whether this should be upgraded from RECOMMENDED to BLOCKING, even though prior reviews kept it at RECOMMENDED since it only seems to matter after the cut.

Since MSA-33 is a save-gating rule on the critical path of D54, a wrong implementation (calling detach_preview on an already-CUT seam, getting an empty result, and having venting incorrectly evaluate false) could let a save fire mid-decompression and violate D54 — a plausible failure mode even though the fix is straightforward. Given this is now the third consecutive report on this issue, I'm leaning toward keeping it RECOMMENDED but flagging it for promotion if unresolved next pass, while checking whether any other blockers remain outstanding.

For Q_MIN, the prior review explicitly said the fix would land this pass, and it didn't — that's now five consecutive reports of what's supposedly a one-line change, which smells like a process failure even though nothing here technically makes implementation wrong or impossible at the shipped defaults. The registry comment defers this until the Assembly owner conforms, and Graph D.14 already uses the max form with build assertions allowing BREACH_HP greater than LEAK_HP. I'm weighing whether to keep this RECOMMENDED per the strict "implement-wrong/impossible" rule, or promote to BLOCKING to force resolution given the tunable values (BREACH_HP 6000, LEAK_HP 4000) can produce a seam that starts already breached with a hole at the weld.

Confirmed: the clamp only triggers if WELD_Q_DEFAULT drops below BREACH_HP/10, which never happens at the default value, so RECOMMENDED is the right call.
