findings.section: Formulas D.1 (L536); MSA-13 (L222); T17 (L1131); FB-8 (L1621); AC-MSA-18 (L1671); registry weld_quality (L5138, pending note L5145)
findings.finding: Q_MIN is still max(400, ceil(LEAK_HP/10)). Graph L735 and LSG D.14 already use max(400, ceil(max(LEAK_HP, BREACH_HP)/10)), and the registry carries an explicit pending note saying it declines until Assembly conforms. BREACH_HP is tunable 1000-6000 against LEAK_HP 4000, and the Graph's build assertions allow BREACH_HP above LEAK_HP. In that range a minimum-quality weld starts BREACHED with no tell, which breaks LSG D.14's 'a fresh seam never starts in LEAK or BREACH'. Outputs are identical at every registry default, and the Graph's own AC (L1228) tests only the defaults, so this is not a pass/fail conflict yet and stays RECOMMENDED. Fifth consecutive report; the fix pass never landed it (G3).
findings.fix: Rewrite D.1 to Q_MIN = max(400, ceil(max(LEAK_HP, BREACH_HP)/10)). Add BREACH_HP to the variables table and to T18. Update T17, FB-8 and MSA-13 to cite D.1. Add a fixture to AC-MSA-18: BREACH_HP 5000 with LEAK_HP 4000 and WELD_Q_DEFAULT 400 gives q 500 with MSA_Q_CLAMPED once. Then edit the registry weld_quality expression and delete the 'pending' comment. Grep for 'ceil(LEAK_HP' afterwards to confirm no copy remains (G3).

findings.section: MSA-33 (L341); D.9 ragged_breach_open row (L766); D.2 keep_sections (L593, L605); Dependencies L1 (L1090); AC-MSA-76/130
findings.finding: venting(s) and ports_open(s) filter on keep_sections(s), which is sourced from Layout detach_preview. Layout L337 defines detach_preview as the LM3 components computed without mutation, so it only exists for an ACTIVE seam. ragged_breach_open() is evaluated only on a CUT seam, including after a restore. No persisted source for the keep side is named, so an implementer would call detach_preview on a CUT seam, get nothing, and find venting false. The event save would then fire mid-decompression, contradicting D54. Third report.
findings.fix: Define the keep side after the cut as the cut_sides entries whose section_id currently belongs to the seam's surviving body. That body is the one holding origin_section_id (LY-17) and is the lower body_id. It is a pure read of layout.state. Reserve detach_preview/keep_sections for seam_cut_offer (pre-cut) only. Add an AC: save at t_cut + 600, restore, and ragged_breach_open() is recomputed from the restored state alone.

findings.section: MSA-33 exposure bound (L341)
findings.finding: The worst-case venting expression is mistyped: ceil(ln(10) x V_total x 1000 / (2 x 24 x 1000)) cancels the 1000s and evaluates to 6, not the stated 5757 steps (34 542 ticks). The number is right because k = G_OPEN x A_CUT / (V x GAS_SCALE) gives 5756.5 for V_total 120, but the written expression is wrong. A programmer coding it as printed gets a 6-step bound. Second report.
findings.fix: Write ceil(ln(10) x V_total x GAS_SCALE / (G_OPEN x A_CUT)) with GAS_SCALE 1000, G_OPEN 2 and A_CUT 24. That gives 2.302585 x 120 x 1000 / 48 = 5756.5, so 5757 steps and 34 542 ticks. Then grep for the old expression everywhere.

findings.finding: There are three inconsistencies. (1) E-31 opens with 'it is not written' and MSA-33 (e) says 'no autosave of either kind is written inside the window', but the same text and AC-MSA-130 say an interval save fires RISKY(ASSEMBLY_BREACH) after AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS 7200. (2) A Save & Quit mid-vent is written RISKY(ASSEMBLY_BREACH). Under R15 a QUIT generation without VITALS in risky_cause is exempt from the fairness step-back. A Continue therefore restores a mid-decompression world, and a death-restart can pick the same QUIT again. Assembly states neither this consequence nor a test for it. (3) AC-MSA-130 (ii) passes on a suit reserve the fixture pins, not on a derived bound. The earlier 'restored world is never mid-decompression' claim in (i) is scoped to the first generation after t_vac and so does not cover the QUIT case.
findings.fix: Reword E-31 and MSA-33 (e) to 'no event save, and no interval save before the 7200 cap'. State the QUIT consequence explicitly: Continue of a mid-vent QUIT restores a vented-or-venting room. Add an AC for QUIT mid-vent, then Continue, then death: restore the same QUIT, and the scripted player can still exit. Derive the winnability bound in (ii) as the time to walk from the far wall to the door against the suit reserve, as a formula, not a pinned number.

findings.section: Formulas D.1 (L536); MSA-13 (L222); T17 (L1131); FB-8 (L1621); AC-MSA-18 (L1671); registry weld_quality (L5138, pending note L5145)

Fifth consecutive report; the fix pass never landed it (G3).

findings.section: MSA-33 (L341); D.9 ragged_breach_open row (L766); D.2 keep_sections (L593, L605); Dependencies L1 (L1090); AC-MSA-76/130
findings.finding: venting(s) and ports_open(s) filter on keep_sections(s), which is sourced from Layout detach_preview. Layout L337 defines detach_preview as the LM3 components computed without mutation, so it only exists for an ACTIVE seam. ragged_breach_open() is evaluated only on a CUT seam, including after a restore. No persisted source for the keep side is named, so an implementer would call detach_preview on a CUT seam, get nothing, and find venting false. The event save would then fire mid-decompression, contradicting D54. Third report.

That body is the one holding origin_section_id (LY-17) and is the lower body_id. It is a pure read of layout.state. Reserve detach_preview/keep_sections for seam_cut_offer (pre-cut) only. findings.section: MSA-33 exposure bound (L341)
findings.finding: The worst-case venting expression is mistyped: ceil(ln(10) x V_total x 1000 / (2 x 24 x 1000)) cancels the 1000s and evaluates to 6, not the stated 5757 steps (34 542 ticks). Second report.
findings.fix: Write ceil(ln(10) x V_total x GAS_SCALE / (G_OPEN x A_CUT)) with GAS_SCALE 1000, G_OPEN 2 and A_CUT 24. That gives 2.302585 x 120 x 1000 / 48 = 5756.5, so 5757 steps and 34 542 ticks. Then grep for the old expression everywhere.

findings.finding: There are three inconsistencies. (1) E-31 opens with 'it is not written' and MSA-33 (e) says 'no autosave of either kind is written inside the window', but the same text and AC-MSA-130 say an interval save fires RISKY(ASSEMBLY_BREACH) after AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS 7200. (2) A Save & Quit mid-vent is written RISKY(ASSEMBLY_BREACH). Under R15 a QUIT generation without VITALS in risky_cause is exempt from the fairness step-back. A Continue therefore restores a mid-decompression world, and a death-restart can pick the same QUIT again. Assembly states neither this consequence nor a test for it. (3) AC-MSA-130 (ii) passes on a suit reserve the fixture pins, not on a derived bound. The earlier 'restored world is never mid-decompression' claim in (i) is scoped to the first generation after t_vac and so does not cover the QUIT case.
findings.fix: Reword E-31 and MSA-33 (e) to 'no event save, and no interval save before the 7200 cap'. State the QUIT consequence explicitly: Continue of a mid-vent QUIT restores a vented-or-venting room. Add an AC for QUIT mid-vent, then Continue, then death: restore the same QUIT, and the scripted player can still exit. Derive the winnability bound in (ii) as the time to walk from the far wall to the door against the suit reserve, as a formula, not a pinned number.

findings.section: AC-MSA-61 (L1757) and AC-MSA-64 (L1762)
findings.finding: The restore-equivalence tests compare restored and uninterrupted state_hash at every tick. Under R1/R13/R14 each restore advances restore_epoch, and threat draws depend on it. Assembly never mentions restore_epoch (0 hits), so the fixture does not say whether the epoch is pinned or no threat systems run. Without that, the equality cannot be guaranteed if Attention or Horror draw in the script.
findings.fix: Add to AC-61 and AC-64: the fixture pins restore_epoch (a Continue of a QUIT generation carries it unchanged, R13) or runs with no Attention/Horror draw sources. Assert the epoch value in the test output.
